subject: CloudNova private offer: minimum usage floor, overage escrow and reseller protection
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@cloudnova.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cloudnova.com
Date: 2026-12-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private offer questions — minimum guarantee & channel protection

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to get clearer on a few items before we move to internal approval:

- Can Redwood accept a minimum-usage guarantee (12-month) with an explicit usage floor that triggers credits if we underutilize?
- We sell through multiple resellers. We need a clause that protects our reseller pass-through (no double-discounting) and a simple mechanism for overage credits if usage spikes beyond forecast that involve resellers.
- Any preference on escrow for overage credits or should we accept a vendor-managed holdback?

I attached the short RFI (CloudNova_Pricing_RFI.xlsx) showing our expected monthly token ranges and initial reseller list. Can you share viability and any redlines we should expect?

Best,
Sanjay
Head of Procurement, CloudNova
attachments: CloudNova_Pricing_RFI.xlsx

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@cloudnova.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-03T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private offer questions — minimum guarantee & channel protection

Sanjay —

Thanks for the RFI and the clear bullets. Short answer: yes, we can model a minimum-usage guarantee and support reseller protection — with a couple of guardrails. High-level:

1) Usage floor: we can accept a 12-month minimum guarantee. We typically structure it as an annual committed spend with monthly reporting and a quarterly reconciliation. If actual usage < floor, we issue pro-rated credits against future consumption (not cash refunds). Credits expire within 12 months.

2) Overage/holdback: for spikes above forecast, we prefer a managed holdback account (vendor-managed ledger) rather than formal escrow in most cases. Escrow is possible for large, regulated customers, but it adds legal and operations overhead. For your case, a vendor-managed overage escrow (tiered release based on monthly reconciliation) seems more pragmatic.

3) Reseller protection: we can add a clause preventing double-discounting and requiring evidence for reseller pass-through claims. We recommend a monthly file-based attestation from resellers and a cap on retroactive credits to avoid open-ended liabilities.

I've looped in Ben (sales ops) and Naomi (finance) to confirm precise credit windows and the typical language we put in PO terms. If this sounds good, we'll put a draft PO with proposed credit cadence and sample language for reseller attestations.

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: RN-PrivateOffer-Terms-draft.pdf

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-04T08:23:00-08:00
Subject: RE: CloudNova private offer — credit cadence + reseller evidence

Mateo / Naomi —

Quick notes from ops & channel perspective:

- Credit cadence: quarterly reconciliation with monthly reporting is the sweet spot. It gives procurement timely visibility and reduces admin overhead.
- Credit expiry: 12 months post-issuance is standard internally. We can extend to 18 months if CloudNova insists, but that affects revenue accounting — finance will need to backlog some.
- Evidence for reseller pass-through: we should require (1) reseller invoice to CloudNova showing the pass-through discount, and (2) a reconciliation CSV every month containing reseller account IDs + usage. We can accept signed attestations for the first 3 months while integrations are stood up.

Also flag: If CloudNova wants formal escrow we need legal to scope. Estimate +2 weeks signoff.

Ben Carter
Director, Deal Ops

On Dec 4, 2026, at 08:50, naomi_feldman@redwood.com wrote:
> Ben — finance thumbs: longer credit lifespans materially change revenue recognition. If we push expiry to 18 months we need to accrue a contra balance that affects recognized ARR. Pragmatically, offer 12 months standard + one-time exception for strategic deals (exec signoff).

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@cloudnova.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Emily Wong <emily.wong@cloudnova.com>, procurement@cloudnova.com
Date: 2026-12-04T10:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private offer questions — minimum guarantee & channel protection

Mateo / Ben / Naomi —

Thanks for the quick turn. A couple of clarifying points from our side after internal review:

- CloudNova needs credits that can be applied retroactively against any future consumption across our main account and not tied solely to a single sub-account (our resellers sometimes route through sub-accounts). Is that feasible?
- For reseller evidence, monthly CSV + signed attestation for the first quarter is acceptable. After quarter 1 we'd expect API-based reporting (simple S3 drop) to avoid manual work.
- On expiry: 12 months is ok, but we would like a provisioning step in the PO that allows a one-time extension to 18 months with mutual written consent (we don't expect to use it but want the flexibility).

If you can produce a one-page term summary with these points we can run to legal and procurement. Also we prefer vendor-managed overage holdback (less legal friction) but are requesting a 30% cap on any one-month retroactive credit to limit exposure to large spikes.

Best,
Sanjay

Subject: Re: Private offer questions — minimum guarantee & channel protection

Sanjay —

Thanks — appreciate the clarity. Attached is a one-page term summary that reflects the items you flagged plus conservative guardrails from our side:

- Annual committed spend = usage floor; monthly reporting + quarterly reconciliation.
- Credit application: credits can be applied across the parent account and any sub-accounts you nominate at signing. We'll add language to allow reassignment by written request (to handle reseller routing).
- Credit expiry: 12 months standard; PO may include a one-time extension to 18 months by mutual written consent (exec-level signoff).
- Overage holdback: vendor-managed ledger preferred. We'll include a 30% per-month retroactive credit cap for any single billing period, and a mechanism to escalate larger one-off events to a dispute process.
- Reseller evidence: initial 3 months attestation OK. After that we expect a monthly CSV or S3 drop. We'll include sample CSV schema in the appendix.

I've attached RN-PrivateOffer-Terms-draft.pdf with the summary and suggested PO language. If CloudNova is aligned I can route to legal and get an estimate on timeline for formal PO + private offer creation in AWS/GCP marketplaces.

Next steps: If you approve the one-pager, reply with "approve terms" and list the sub-accounts that should receive credit flexibility. We'll target a draft PO within 7 business days once legal scope is agreed.

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: RN-PrivateOffer-Terms-draft.pdf
